properties.name: vanillabp.prioritized-adapters
properties.description: Adapter IDs ordered by priority. New workflows are started using the first adapter; other actions target the BPMS the workflow is running in. Each item has to be a key of 'vanillabp.adapters'. May be omitted if exactly one adapter is configured. Overridable per workflow module ('vanillabp.workflow-modules.<id>.prioritized-adapters').

properties.name: vanillabp.resources-location
properties.description: Where to load VanillaBP BPMN files from, which are NOT specific to any adapter (e.g. 'classpath*:processes'). Adapter-specific BPMN is configured per workflow module at 'vanillabp.workflow-modules.<module>.adapters.<id>.resources-location'.

properties.name: vanillabp.adapters
properties.description: The configuration of all adapters known, keyed by adapter ID. The ID can be an adapter's type or a custom identifier - in the latter case 'type' has to name the adapter type. Besides the platform keys ('type', 'deployment-failure') each BPMS adapter contributes its own keys to its section (e.g. connection settings).

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.poll-interval
properties.description: The fixed delay between two background polls for committed-but-unprocessed outbox entries. Polling is required for crash recovery and retries; right after a commit the entry is dispatched immediately (independently of this delay).

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.attempt-frequency
properties.description: How long to wait after a failed dispatch until the entry is retried.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.max-attempt-frequency
properties.description: The longest distance the growing backoff reaches. Every failed attempt doubles the wait until it arrives here, so a BPMS which comes back is noticed within this period however long it was away. The gruelbox store knows one fixed distance and does not follow this key.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.block-after-attempts
properties.description: After how many failed attempts an entry is blocked (not retried any longer). Blocked entries have to be fixed manually (e.g. by cleaning up the outbox store).

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.dispatch-threads
properties.description: How many entries an outbox of VanillaBP's own dispatches at the same time. The workflow aggregate decides which thread takes an entry, so two operations of one workflow keep the order they were written in. Every dispatch costs a database connection and a call to the BPMS, so a large number here only moves the limit into the connection pool.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.create-schema
properties.description: Whether the schema (table/collection) used to store outbox entries is created automatically. Disable this if the database schema is managed manually (e.g. by Flyway or Liquibase).

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.retention
properties.description: How long successfully dispatched entries (marked as DONE) are retained before they are deleted asynchronously. What a retained entry buys is a dispatched operation somebody can still look at during support. It does not widen the deduplication window: that one ends with the dispatch. The records of processed task deliveries are kept for a period of their own, 'vanillabp.delivery.retention'.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.jdbc.enabled
properties.description: Whether the JDBC-based default outbox is created when a data source is available. Disable it if the application defines its own PhaseTwoOutbox bean and the default (including its store and background dispatcher) is unwanted.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.jdbc.table
properties.description: The name of the table storing outbox entries (default 'VANILLABP_PHASE_TWO_OUTBOX'). An application which switched to gruelbox ('vanillabp.outbox.gruelbox.enabled') stores its entries in gruelbox' own table 'TXNO_OUTBOX'. This key does not rename that table, but the payloads of that store follow the name written here. Every outbox instance needs its own store - two dispatchers polling the same table would compete and double-dispatch.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.jdbc.payload-table
properties.description: The name of the table storing the payloads of phase-two calls which carry one. Unset means the name of the outbox table plus '_PAYLOAD', so an application which renames the outbox renames the payloads with it. One table per outbox, for the reason the outbox itself has one: two applications sharing it would house-keep each other's rows.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.jdbc.delivery-table
properties.description: The name of the table storing the records of processed task deliveries (default 'VANILLABP_TASK_DELIVERY'). Unlike the payload table it does not follow a renamed outbox: the delivery log is a store of its own. An application which sets it applies the same name to 'io.vanillabp:vanillabp-schema', through the changelog property 'vanillabp.delivery.table'.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.jdbc.housekeeping-table
properties.description: The name of the table the nightly housekeeping takes its lease in (default 'VANILLABP_HOUSEKEEPING') - one row per store, holding who is house-keeping it and until when, so only one node of a cluster measures its own work. Like the delivery table it does not follow a renamed outbox. An application which sets it applies the same name to 'io.vanillabp:vanillabp-schema', through the changelog property 'vanillabp.housekeeping.table'.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.mongo.enabled
properties.description: Whether the MongoDB-based default outbox is created when a MongoDB connection is available. Disable it if the application defines its own PhaseTwoOutbox bean and the default (including its store and background dispatcher) is unwanted.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.mongo.collection
properties.description: The name of the collection storing outbox entries. Every outbox instance needs its own store - two dispatchers polling the same collection would compete and double-dispatch.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.mongo.payload-collection
properties.description: The name of the collection storing the payloads of phase-two calls which carry one. Unset means the name of the outbox collection plus '-payloads', so an application which renames the outbox renames the payloads with it. One collection per outbox, for the reason the outbox itself has one.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.mongo.delivery-collection
properties.description: The name of the collection storing the records of processed task deliveries. Keep it apart from the outbox collection and from the payload collection: stores sharing one collection read each other's documents. How long a record is kept is 'vanillabp.delivery.retention'.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.mongo.housekeeping-collection
properties.description: The name of the collection the nightly housekeeping takes its lease in - one document per store, holding who is house-keeping it and until when, so only one node of a cluster measures its own work. Keep it apart from the other three collections.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.housekeeping.start
properties.description: When the nightly housekeeping of the outbox opens its window. Inside it the entries whose retention passed and the payloads no entry names are removed, as much as fits; outside it neither costs anything. A window whose end lies before its start crosses midnight.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.housekeeping.end
properties.description: When the housekeeping window closes. It is a deadline and not a promise: a batch which is running then runs to its end, and the next one does not start. Widen it where 'vanillabp.outbox.housekeeping.remaining' stays above zero.

properties.name: vanillabp.outbox.housekeeping.zone
properties.description: The time zone the housekeeping window is read in, written the way ZoneId spells one (e.g. 'Europe/Vienna'). Unset means the zone of the JVM - and a JVM standing on UTC without this key ends the startup, because 'four in the morning' would then mean four UTC. Write 'UTC' here if that is what you mean.

properties.name: vanillabp.conventional-resources-locations
properties.description: Where the BPMN files of a workflow module lie when no 'resources-location' names a place. VanillaBP derives it from the classpath while it boots, so it is not a key an application writes.

deprecation.reason: Derived from the classpath by VanillaBP while it boots, so a value written here is replaced. Write 'vanillabp.resources-location' or 'vanillabp.workflow-modules.<module>.adapters.<adapter>.resources-location' instead.

properties.name: vanillabp.retired-adapters
properties.description: Adapter IDs this application does not serve any more, the last step of a BPMS migration. An outbox entry or a delivery record still naming one of them is reported at startup, because an unserved id usually means the id was renamed and workflows were lost. Naming it here says the leftovers are known and turns that message into a DEBUG line.

properties.name: vanillabp.extensions
properties.description: What the extensions of the deployment pipeline are configured with, keyed by extension id. What the keys below an extension mean is that extension's own business. Overridable per workflow module, per workflow, per task and per adapter section of each of those levels.

properties.name: vanillabp.allow-full-sync-with-bpms
properties.description: Bound so that a line here is answered instead of ignored: the permission to hand a whole workflow aggregate to the BPMS belongs to the single workflow, at 'vanillabp.workflow-modules.<module>.workflows.<bpmn-process-id>.allow-full-sync-with-bpms'. Written here it ends the startup with a message naming that key. A permission taken from above would cover the workflow somebody adds next week.

properties.name: vanillabp.delivery.release-on-workflow-end
properties.description: Whether the records of a workflow are deleted the moment it ends, instead of waiting for 'vanillabp.delivery.retention' to pass. The end of an instance is the one moment after which nothing of it can be redelivered, so the deletion is safe. It is off by default because the end of a workflow is reported only where the application asked for it, so switching it on makes every deployed model of the module carry the listener reporting that end. Overridable per workflow module.

properties.name: vanillabp.delivery.max-task-age
properties.description: How long a task may stay open before VanillaBP reports it, counted from the moment its handler ran. A task left open by a @TaskId handler is a task the application promised to complete later, and nothing else asks whether that promise was kept. '0' switches the report off. Overridable per workflow module, per workflow and per task.

properties.name: vanillabp.delivery.check-open-tasks-on-delivery
properties.description: Whether a delivery looks at the other tasks VanillaBP believes are open in the same workflow, asks the BPMS whether they still exist and reports the ones which are gone as canceled. Only a method which asked for the event with a @TaskEvent parameter is affected, and on a BPMS which cannot say per element what it took away this is the only way such a method is ever called. Overridable per workflow module, per workflow and per task.

properties.name: vanillabp.delivery.max-open-tasks-checked
properties.description: How many other open tasks one delivery probes at most, oldest record first. What is not reached this time is reached at the next wake-up of that workflow. Each probe is one call to the BPMS on the thread of the delivery, so this is the cap which keeps a workflow with very many open tasks from holding an execution slot for all of them. '0' switches the probing off. Overridable per workflow module, per workflow and per task.

properties.name: vanillabp.delivery.retention
properties.description: How long the record of a processed task delivery is kept, counted from the last redelivery it answered. This is a correctness setting: a delivery arriving later than this finds no record and runs the @WorkflowTask method a second time, so the period has to cover the longest gap between a handler running and the last redelivery of that work, including however long the application is stopped. Unset means 'vanillabp.outbox.retention', which is where this number lived before the two were told apart.

properties.name: vanillabp.election.guessing-adapters
properties.description: What VanillaBP does about a prioritized adapter which cannot say whether it holds a workflow, next to at least one other adapter: 'rejected' ends the boot with a message naming the adapter and the fix, 'accepted' routes operations on existing workflows by list order instead and logs a warning. Overridable per workflow module.

properties.name: vanillabp.metrics.gauge-cache
properties.description: How long the measurement of a gauge which has to ask somebody is reused before it is taken again. Ten seconds is one collection interval, a little under the fifteen seconds Prometheus scrapes with by default, so every scrape gets a measurement of its own while a dashboard opened next to it reads the number that scrape already paid for. 'PT0S' switches the holding off and every collection measures.

properties.name: vanillabp.transactions.unguarded-aggregate-writes
properties.description: What VanillaBP does about a workflow-aggregate store which its transaction demonstrably does not cover: 'rejected' ends the boot with a message naming the fix, 'accepted' lets the application run with writes which do not commit or roll back together and logs a warning. Overridable per workflow module.

properties.name: vanillabp.workflow-adapter-cache.max-entries
properties.description: How many workflows the cache remembers the adapter of, so an operation on a known workflow does not ask every BPMS again. The oldest entry goes when the cache is full.

properties.name: vanillabp.workflow-adapter-cache.time-to-live
properties.description: How long the remembered adapter of a running workflow stays valid. A workflow migrated to another BPMS behind VanillaBP's back is found again after this period at the latest.

properties.name: vanillabp.workflow-adapter-cache.ended-time-to-live
properties.description: How long the cache remembers that a workflow has ended. Shorter than the entry of a running one: what an ended workflow saves is the probing of a late call, and nothing about it changes any more.

properties.name: vanillabp.workflow-adapter-cache.release-on-workflow-end
properties.description: Whether the cache entry of a workflow is dropped the moment the BPMS reports that it ended, instead of waiting for 'vanillabp.workflow-adapter-cache.ended-time-to-live'. Like the delivery records, switching it on makes every deployed model of the application carry the listener reporting that end.

properties.name: vanillabp.workflow-modules
properties.description: The properties of all workflow modules, keyed by the workflow module's ID: per-module adapter priorities ('prioritized-adapters') and per-module adapter properties ('adapters.<id>.resources-location' for BPMS-specific BPMN).
